originality.rationale: The exact new statement is a globally sharp positive linear comparison between third and fifth centered moment EXCESSES at fixed first two moments, with a piecewise coefficient. Meer and Weeks state only a weaker endpoint bound as a conjecture and explicitly propose cross-moment comparisons; Rowe 1988 provides scalar transformed-expectation extrema under constant-sign derivatives, but the transformed contrast here violates that derivative condition. The inspected 2023 power-moment paper uses raw moments and does not imply the exact centered slope. Published-record and primary-literature searches found no equivalent claim; priority risk in classical moment-cone literature remains.

value.rationale: The motivating 2023/2024 probability study explicitly calls for moment-order relationships, not just individual moment minima. The theorem quantitatively couples two standard asymmetry statistics under only a nonnegative-support and mean/variance constraint, with a best possible piecewise coefficient and a structural transition at v=3/2; the sharpness construction gives optimality over all laws. It is neither a single arbitrary parameter slice nor a mere normalized fifth-moment endpoint conjecture. Its limitation to a sharp linear comparison (not the complete moment cone) is stated.
